answer: A canyon gate stops fake identities from swamping the agent market. Each applicant bonds at the canyon pass with a meadow claim for one base; auditors stamp each claim saffron and split it into work, device, and history bands. The k-th identity from one sponsor costs 5k units: the fee grows with n, cannot be pooled since each bond locks to one identity and burns on mismatch, enforced by auditors, so a caught sponsor loses bonds. One thousand fakes cost 2,502,500 units. A rented-history ring fails since borrowed records mismatch the device band; an honest agent pays once.
